propositions: Four call sites in the reconciler use cast() to access optional capability members (add_comment, set_relationship) but perform no runtime guards, allowing AttributeError to be silently swallowed by broad exception handlers.
When a transport lacks an opt-in capability, the mutation is never applied but the pass reports success, conflating designed skips with real failures.
isinstance() guards against @runtime_checkable Protocols must be added at all four call sites before capability member access, distinct from the hasattr() pattern in fetcher.py.

Capability-absent events must be logged as INFO with a durable record on the bridge_alerts channel using distinct kinds (outbound-comment-capability-absent, outbound-link-capability-absent) rather than raising or silently failing.

The isinstance check must include a hasattr() fallback for Python 3.11 compatibility, as @runtime_checkable uses getattr_static on 3.12+ but plain hasattr on 3.11, affecting proxy and mock transports.
Module size constraint requires relocating _call_with_retry (~75 LOC) from dispatch_one.py to dispatch_apply_phases.py to stay within the 800-LOC cap after adding guards.
